name: Hot Milk Cake

ingredients.name: cake flour, plus more for dusting

instructions.primary_message: Adjust rack to middle position and preheat oven to 350ºF (175ºC). Grease Bundt pan with unsalted butter, then dust with cake flour, shaking out excess. (See notes.)
In a medium bowl, whisk together cake flour, baking powder, and salt; set aside.
In a large measuring cup, combine milk with vegetable oil.
In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment, whip eggs and granulated sugar on medium-high speed until yolks are thick and pale yellow color, and doubled in volume, about 7 minutes.
Reduce mixer speed to low, and slowly pour in milk and oil mixture. Continue to whisk until combined, about 15 seconds.

With the mixer on low speed, gradually add the dry mixture 1/4 cup at a time, until just incorporated, about 2 minutes. Using a flexible spatula, scrape down sides and bottom of the bowl to ensure there are no dry bits. (If any remain, use spatula to gently fold until incorporated.) Pour batter into prepared cake pan and gently tap cake pan on kitchen counter 2 to 3 times to eliminate any large air bubbles.

Bake, rotating halfway through, until cake has risen by about 1 inch, is light golden, and springs back when gently touched, 40 to 45 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack and allow cake to cool in pan for 30 minutes.

Carefully invert cake onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Let cool completely, at least 30 minutes. (Cooled cake can be wrapped tightly in plastic wrap and stored at room temperature for up to 24 hours.)

schema_metadata.keywords: hot milk cake, cake with hot milk, hot milk cake recipe

description: The hot milk cake is a tender, airy, exceedingly delicious cake that’s almost as delicate as a chiffon cake or genoise, but with just enough heft to feel like a lighter version of a vanilla butter cake.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 55 min.

Notes: The cake can also be baked in two 9-inch aluminum cake pans. If using two 9-inch aluminum cake pans, line the bottoms of each pan with parchment paper. Grease paper and sides of the pan with unsalted butter, then dust with cake flour, shaking out excess. When batter is prepared, divide evenly between pans (about 1 pound; 454g each). Bake, rotating halfway through, until cake has risen by about 1 inch, is light golden, and springs back when gently touched, 17 to 20 minutes. Transfer pans to a wire rack and allow cakes to cool in pans for 30 minutes.

Make-ahead and storage: The cake can be tightly wrapped in plastic and refrigerated for up to 1 week or frozen for up to 3 months.
author: Genevieve Yam
